newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul airport hit by rockets.
newsitem.headline: Kabul airport hit by rockets.

text.p: Three salvos of rockets from a multiple launcher hit the airport in the Afghan capital Kabul on Saturday morning as an opposition alliance stepped up pressure on the Taleban movement controlling the city, witnesses said.
Moments after the last salvo landed at 10.15 A.M. (0545 GMT), huge clouds of dust, mixed with black smoke from the rockets' high explosive, hung in the air over the airport in northeastern Kabul.

The anti-Taleban alliance moved within rocketing range of Kabul on Thursday when it pushed the Taleban back to within 12 miles (20 km) of the city, which the purist Islamic movement captured last September.
The move put the city within range of the opposition's Soviet-built rocket batteries for the first time in nine months.
Taleban guards denied journalists access to the site, but the rockets seem to have landed at the western end of the airport complex.
It was impossible to assess the extent of damage to the airport, which is used for both military and civilian traffic.

The United Nations and the International Committee of the Red Cross used to use the airport to ferry personnel and supplies into Kabul. Both agencies have suspended flights due to air raids and the rocket attacks.

The rocket attacks increase pressure on the Taleban, who are already hard-pressed on the front lines north of Kabul. In a rapid advance over the past five days the Taleban have lost most of the western side of the Shomali valley.
The Shomali valley runs north from Kabul into the foothills of the Hindu Kush mountain range.
The opposition has moved more than 35 miles (60 km) closer to Kabul, capturing Charikar, the capital of Parwan province 48 miles (75 km) north of the Afghan capital, and the nearby Bagram air base.
